notes.text: Use the large pot instead of the skillet, so all the fish fits in one layer in the sauce.

move.title: Fish cooked in a barely bubbling sauce
move.body: Poaching means cooking food gently in liquid that's hot but not boiling. Today you'll build a garlicky tomato sauce with olives and capers, nestle pieces of cod into it, and poach them with the lid on until they turn white and flake apart, then serve the fish and sauce together.

callback.body: In shakshuka, eggs cooked gently in a simmering tomato sauce under a lid. Cod works the same way: the sauce is the cooking liquid, and it flavors the fish while it cooks.

why.title: A soft onion base
why.body: The onion is sweated on medium-low until soft and sweet, the Unit 4 way, so it melts into the sauce.

why.title: Thicken the sauce first
why.body: The fish gives off juice as it cooks. A sauce simmered thick first stays thick; a thin one turns watery.

why.title: Hot, not boiling
why.body: Poaching liquid sits around 160 to 180°F, with only a bubble now and then. A hard boil tosses the fish around, breaks it apart, and toughens the outside before the middle is done.

why.title: Olives and capers bring the salt
why.body: Olives and capers are packed in brine, so they add salt as well as flavor. Taste the sauce after they go in, before you add any more salt.

why.title: 145°F, and it flakes
why.body: Cooked cod turns from see-through to solid white and separates into big flakes when you press it with a fork. The thermometer in the thickest piece should read 145°F.

wrong.fix: The sauce was bubbling too hard, or the fish was moved too much. It still tastes good; next time keep the heat low and leave it alone.
Lift the fish out onto a plate, simmer the sauce with the lid off for 5 minutes, then spoon it back over.
Stir in a few spoonfuls of water and a squeeze of lemon. Next time, taste after the olives and capers before adding salt.

wrong.sign: The thick pieces aren't done but the thin ones are
wrong.fix: Move the thin pieces to a warm plate and give the thick ones 2 more minutes.

quiz.q: What does poaching liquid look like?
choices: Hot, with only a bubble now and then
quiz.explain: A hard boil breaks the fish apart.

quiz.q: Why simmer the sauce thick before the fish goes in?
choices: The fish gives off juice that thins it

quiz.q: Why taste before adding more salt?

substitutions.note: Tilapia is thinner. Start checking at 6 minutes.

steps.text: Dice the onion into ¼-inch cubes. Peel the garlic and slice it thin. Cut the olives in half.
steps.tip: Use the claw, knuckles against the blade.

steps.text: Warm the oil in the skillet over medium-low heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring now and then, until it's soft and see-through.
steps.look: Soft and shiny, with no brown edges.

steps.text: Add the garlic, and the chili flakes if you're using them, and stir for 1 minute until it smells good.

Pour in the tomatoes slowly, close to the pan. Add the olives, capers, oregano, and the sauce's salt. Bring it to a bubble, then turn the heat down and simmer with the lid off, stirring now and then, until it's thick.
steps.look: A spoon dragged across the pan leaves a path for a second.

steps.text: Taste the sauce. It may already be salty enough from the olives and capers.
Lay the cod on the plate, pat it dry with paper towels, and sprinkle it with the fish's salt. Nestle each piece into the sauce, and spoon a little sauce over the top.
Throw the paper towels and the fish's package away. Put the plate in the sink, and wash your hands with soap.
Put the lid on and turn the heat to low. Poach the fish without stirring.
steps.look: Only a bubble now and then around the fish, never a boil.
steps.tip: If it starts to bubble hard, turn the heat down.

steps.text: Slide the thermometer into the side of the thickest piece. It needs to read at least 145°F, and flake when you press it with a fork. If not, put the lid back on and poach 2 more minutes.
Turn off the stove. Scatter the parsley over the top. Lift each piece of fish into a bowl with the spatula, spoon sauce over it, and serve with lemon wedges, and warm pita if you like.
